question.problem:
Calculate the slope of the line shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14166993/assets/48114216e210a4e4dfc353871bbfd16bd2beb480f5831c62189db9299e09f517.png)
question.worked_solution:
Note that the line passes through the points $(-2,0)$ and $(0,2).$ So, we let $(x_1,y_1) = (-2,0)$ and $(x_2,y_2) = (0,2),$ and compute the slope using the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{2-0}{0-(-2)} \\  & =\frac{2}{2} \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the line is $m=1.$
